claims.text: Enhancing chemical short-range order stabilizes the nanoscale microstructure of high-entropy nanoalloys at high temperature.
Enhancing chemical short-range order suppresses high-temperature elemental segregation.
Enhancing chemical short-range order suppresses oxidation at high temperature.
The proposed initial material has a random elemental distribution and a nanocrystalline structure with grain size no greater than 100 nm.
The proposed initial nanoalloy may have a bcc or fcc structure.
Monte Carlo swap treatment can induce chemical short-range order from an initially random alloy configuration.
Low-temperature annealing with controlled cooling can promote short-range order without significantly changing grain size.
Short-range-ordered regions form percolating clusters within the nanoalloy.
Short-range order increases local chemical homogeneity among subsets of elements.
Increased short-range order reduces the thermodynamic driving force for phase separation.
Increased short-range order limits atomic diffusion.
Relative to a random-alloy baseline, an SRO-enhanced nanoalloy will exhibit slower grain growth after high-temperature exposure.
Relative to a random-alloy baseline, an SRO-enhanced nanoalloy will exhibit reduced oxidation depth after high-temperature exposure.
Relative to a random-alloy baseline, an SRO-enhanced nanoalloy will exhibit less elemental segregation after high-temperature exposure.
The prediction is limited to comparable compositions, grain sizes below 100 nm, temperatures of 800–1000 °C, durations around 100 hours, and inert or low-oxygen atmospheres.
Changes in diffusion and oxidation behavior may be on the order of 10–20%.
The controlled comparison is intended to hold composition and initial nanocrystalline grain size constant while varying the SRO-promoting treatment.
